title: I. J. Good and the question of controlling a greater intelligence
summary: I. J. Good helped turn mathematical ideas into tools for wartime codebreaking. He also imagined a machine capable of designing its successor. His biography follows the evidence behind those achievements, the forecast that missed its century and the question that remains: how could people retain meaningful control over an intelligence greater than their own?
author: The Bible of AI

title: An AI finds an equation. What makes it a physical law?
summary: An equation can fit a set of numbers and still fail to describe the physical phenomenon behind them. This article follows an ideal pendulum through two separate questions: whether a proposed expression has compatible units and whether its predictions agree with the evidence. An original example shows why dimensional rules can reject some formulas while admitting others that predict different periods. Research on symbolic regression then explains how learned proposals and explicit constraints can cooperate during the search itself. The discussion distinguishes recovering a known expression from discovering a new law, and reads recent performance claims with their actual denominators, noise conditions and supplied information. The central question is what remains unresolved after an equation has passed a check. Measurements, uncertainty and tests beyond the conditions used to construct a model remain essential to judging what the model can explain.
author: The Bible of AI

title: How does a humanoid robot keep its balance while carrying a box?
summary: When a humanoid lifts a box, the table stops supporting its weight. Holding the box close reduces the turning effect of its weight. To take a step, the robot must manage the change in support as one foot leaves the floor. How does it learn to make that correction? Experiments in Beijing and Oregon trace the path from a camera image and a changing foot load to a new command at a joint. A separate study follows a robot as it lifts a basket from a side platform, carries it to a table and sets it down. The researchers count a success only when the basket rests securely on the tabletop. A robot can stay upright and still fail its delivery. To judge what the AI contributes, we need to know which movements it controls and whether it recovers when the next box carries its weight differently.
author: The Bible of AI

title: Ilya Sutskever and the pursuit of safe superintelligence
summary: Ilya Sutskever helped machines recognise images and translate sentences before co-founding OpenAI. His next undertaking, Safe Superintelligence Inc., places a harder question at the centre of its mission: how can people control systems more capable than themselves? This biography follows the shared scientific achievements, the departure from OpenAI and the evidence behind SSI’s evolving strategy.

title: ‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?
summary: The one thing stopping AI taking over the world – or at least everyone’s jobs? Dexterity. Human hands are anatomical marvels that engineers have struggled for years to replicate. Experts are racing to change that Just outside Luton, in an Amazon warehouse the size of four football pitches, yellow shelving units pirouette in a digitally choreographed dance. Tubs containing a Lego Spider-Man kit, followed by dishwasher tablets, followed by a pouch of muscle building protein powder whiz along conveyor belts, until they arrive at a human being tasked with stacking the shelving unit that has come to a stop in front of their workstation. This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success. Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up its fulfilment centres to carefully controlled free public tours a decade ago. Our guide tells us about the competitive rates of pay Amazon workers receive, their pensions, dental cover and options for flexible working. Her delivery is somewhat robotic. Continue reading...
